research_concepts: role transferability across contexts (regular season to playoffs)
play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points)
methodological_questions: Can 'role travel' be defined and measured for shaper profiles before any test is run?
Can cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper profiles be labelled reliably from the play-by-play data?
Is n=24 units enough to compare role travel between shaper types at useful power?
Which labelling, exposure, selection and drift risks threaten a test of role travel?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type labelling audit found OTHER possessions ending in fouls about 36% of the time, inflating OTHER PPP (FOUL_BUCKET). DRIVE sat 12pp below the foul benchmark (FOUL_LEAK). Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict: artifact_found.

Play-type label accuracy audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% of labels low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types above benchmark PPP band, MIA identity checks failed. Verdict: tool_eval_fail.

Play-type cross-possession memory check failed decay-sanity. DRIVE lifts were flat (+0.015 to +0.021 across lags), Cohen d about 0.01-0.03, p near 0 from n>150k, and the within-team baseline collapsed the effect. Team quality was a confound. Verdict: failed_gate.

Regular season vs playoff PPP by play type: DRIVE RS 1.198 vs PO 0.912 (-0.286, 25 teams, min 30 possessions per cell, no CIs). PNR -0.173, PULL_UP +0.301, others within -0.07. Used to motivate the playoff DRIVE exclusion. This is team-level, not shaper-level, evidence.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1197 pooled records, no CIs): DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060), CUT +0.114, PNR +0.087, PULL_UP -0.077, POST_UP -0.032. Recorded as no clear signal for DRIVE declining across series, with selection caveats.

Similar-profile teammate vs absorb/cascade when a player sits: mean similarity ABSORBED +0.863 vs CASCADE +0.848, Spearman(sim, -gap) = -0.19 (wrong-signed). Recorded failure type is B_powered_null, but sample/power is NOT_RECORDED and the verdict is null, so the record is internally inconsistent on power.
Player BEST/AVOID tier tendency across 55 series (179 players, 25 teams, min 10 possessions). Descriptive only, with team AVOID% ranging 6.8% to 50.6%.
Memoryless Monte Carlo possession simulation (10,000 games x 200 possessions). Generative check only; sequence R2 about 0 by construction. Not independent evidence.
Joint vs sequential Rank-then-Route ranking (n=2,779 triggers): joint pick matched sequential in 80.3%, mean PPP left on table +0.020 overall. Descriptive.
Player routing V4 vs V5 direct scoring: 8 divergences, 0 scoreable (players missing from the graph). Hit rate not computable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using initiation_type-based play-type labels to compare play-type PPP and profiles
failed_approaches.why: Only 0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type; OTHER was inflated by foul endings. Recorded as artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type label accuracy and distribution audit used as a base for adaptation findings
failed_approaches.why: Audit failed on OTHER share, low-confidence labels, foul-draw benchmarks and team identity checks (label error and leakage recorded). Verdict tool_eval_fail.
Flat lifts with no decay; collapsed under within-team baseline; team-quality confounding. Recorded as failed_gate.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Player routing V4 vs V5 comparison
failed_approaches.why: Zero scoreable divergences (8 unscored because players were missing from the graph); recorded as untestable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Similarity of a teammate's play-type profile as a separator of absorption from cascade
failed_approaches.why: Wrong-signed relation (Spearman -0.19) and almost-always-findable similar teammates; label error recorded as a limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing whether DRIVE PPP declines across playoff series
failed_approaches.why: No clear signal; observational with selection and regression-to-the-mean caveats; no CIs.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels derived from the available play-by-play have documented validity failures (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014), so any cut-heavy vs drive-heavy profile built on them is unreliable until audited.

Regular-season vs playoff PPP differs by play type at team level, with DRIVE lower in the playoffs by about 0.29 in one 25-team sample (FAM:SF-APPS-011). This is a team-level, not shaper-level, finding without CIs.

Earlier attempts to find cross-possession or series-level play-type effects were null, artifact or inconclusive (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-010), so a naive role-travel test is likely to repeat these problems.
No returned record tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy shapers' roles.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether cut-heavy shaper profiles are a valid, reliable category in the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data.
Whether any role or shaper-level property transfers from regular season to playoffs, or differs by shaper type.
Effect sizes with confidence intervals for the cut vs drive contrast; the retrieved PPP differences carry no CIs.
Any power calculation for n=24 units. Retrieved records give no power analysis for this question.
How 'role travel' should be operationalised. No record defines it.
own_inferences: 'Travel' is undefined. Without a fixed operational definition (for example, a profile's stability across RS, PO or seasons), the question cannot be falsified.

With 24 units, a cut-heavy vs drive-heavy contrast would need a very large effect to reach useful power, and the team-level DRIVE RS/PO effect in FAM:SF-APPS-011 is too unstable (no CIs, 25 teams) to serve as a planning effect size.
Mixing regular-season and playoff contexts confounds role travel with rotation, opponent quality and sample-size changes (playoff games are fewer and more selected).
Because DRIVE playoff exclusion was motivated by FAM:SF-APPS-011, DRIVE-based profiles in the playoffs may be partly determined by an earlier design decision, which would create circularity.
uncertainties: The retrieval set does not include any record on cut-heavy shaper profiles, shaper-level role measures or role transfer as such; relevance is inferred from play-type and series-level records only.
The unit count is 24 in the task, but several records use 25 teams. The reason for the discrepancy is not recorded here and needs checking.
FAM:SF-CHT-052 is internally inconsistent (status inconclusive, failure type B_powered_null, power NOT_RECORDED), so its power cannot be relied on.
No validation status is recorded for any retrieved record (all no_validation_recorded), so none of the results is independently confirmed.
The retrieval set was limited to ten records; no follow-up search was run.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the retrieved evidence, the question might have looked testable as a straightforward play-type comparison. The records show play-type labels fail audit (FAM:SF-CHT-025, FAM:SF-APPM-014), prior play-type effects were artifacts or inconclusive (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-010), and several analyses were untestable or lacked power (FAM:SF-APPS-009, FAM:SF-CHT-052). This moved the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed as posed, with a label-audit prerequisite.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels derived from play-by-play fail audit (0.7% mapping via initiation_type; OTHER foul leakage; low-confidence labels) per FAM:SF-CHT-025 and FAM:SF-APPM-014. Shaper profiles built on these labels are not valid.
n=24 units is unlikely to give useful power for a cut vs drive contrast in role transfer, and the recorded effects have no CIs.
'Role travel' and 'cut-heavy' or 'drive-heavy' shaper profiles have no defined, validated measure; no reliability evidence is recorded.
Comparing regular season with playoffs (and across 2022-23 to 2025-26) mixes contexts and seasons; FAM:SF-APPS-011 shows the DRIVE effect differs by context.
Team quality, opponent, rotation and playoff selection confound any role-travel comparison, as in FAM:SF-CHT-029.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy shapers'. Related prior work covers play-type label validity (artifact and tool_eval_fail), a team-level RS vs playoff DRIVE PPP drop (supported, no CIs), series-level DRIVE trends (inconclusive), and a similar-teammate absorb/cascade test (inconclusive, power unclear). These address components of the question, not the question itself.

risks.text: Play-type labels are unreliable (FAM:SF-CHT-025: 0.7% mapping; FAM:SF-APPM-014: OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence). Cut and drive shares may be misclassified, and foul endings may contaminate OTHER.
If shaper profiles are defined using points or PPP, the profile and the outcome are not independent, which would bias any role-travel comparison.
24 units is small. Any contrast between cut-heavy and drive-heavy groups will be underpowered unless the effect is very large, and multiple cut and drive contrasts increase false-positive risk.
Playoff exposure is limited (fewer games, selected teams), so playoff role measures per shaper may be sparse, as with the minimum-cell rules in FAM:SF-APPS-011 and FAM:SF-APPS-015.
No reliability estimate exists for shaper profile or role measures; year-to-year and RS-to-PO stability is unknown.
Team quality, opponent strength, rotation and minutes confound role travel. FAM:SF-CHT-029 showed a team-quality confound collapsing an apparent effect.
Seasons 2022-23 to 2025-26 and RS vs playoffs differ in play-type mix and PPP; pooling without adjustment would mix regimes.

Selecting extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy shapers and then measuring their role in another context will overstate contrasts through regression to the mean; FAM:SF-APPS-010 flagged selection and regression-to-the-mean limits.
Many play types, contexts and seasons (as in the retrieved families) invite post hoc contrasts without correction.
Generative or simulated baselines (FAM:SF-APPS-071) are not independent evidence; placebo checks must not rely on constructed sequences.

design.estimand: Not estimable as posed. Minimum viable estimand: within-shaper change in a pre-defined play-type profile (cut share vs drive share, with labels audited) between regular season and playoffs, comparing shaper groups defined before outcomes are seen.
design.unit: Shaper-season (player within team-season), with team-context as a random effect. Not used at the team level alone.
design.sample: Not established. The task lists 24 units; the retrieved records describe 25 teams. Reconcile before any test. A minimum viable pre-registration would first audit labels on a holdout set of games and report the mapping rate and foul-leakage rate.
design.power: Not computed. With n=24 units, power for cut vs drive contrasts is expected to be low unless the effect is very large. A power analysis must be run before any test, using CI widths from FAM:SF-APPS-011 as a starting point, and the test should be declared underpowered if the planned n cannot detect a pre-specified effect.
design.controls: Team quality (team net rating or opponent-adjusted measure), opponent quality, minutes and rotation, season fixed effects, within-team baselines (as in FAM:SF-CHT-029), and foul-endings handled as a separate category rather than folded into OTHER.
design.falsification: Pre-register that a cut-heavy advantage in role transfer is falsified if the within-shaper RS-to-PO change for cut-heavy shapers is not smaller than for drive-heavy shapers, with a CI excluding the pre-specified effect; also pre-register a placebo play type with no hypothesised transfer advantage.
design.multiplicity: Single primary contrast (cut-heavy vs drive-heavy transfer difference). All other play types and contexts are secondary and corrected (for example Holm) or labelled exploratory.
design.decision_rule: Proceed only if (a) label audit passes pre-set thresholds (initiation_type mapping rate, OTHER share, foul-leakage rate) on the holdout, (b) a definition of role travel is fixed and reliability is reported, and (c) the power analysis shows useful power at the planned sample. Otherwise report as untestable or underpowered, not as a null.
design.data_version: NBA 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs as listed. 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13 only; 2025-26 playoffs are complete from 2026-06-21 only. Use only complete data for the pre-registered analysis.

how to define and measure cut-heavy versus drive-heavy shaper profiles from play-by-play
what sample size and exposure is needed to compare role travel between shaper types
which risks (sample size, reliability, selection, label derivation, leakage) threaten a test of role transfer

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}
